faq.q: Why is the left side of the heart stronger?
faq.a: The left ventricle pumps blood all around the body, which needs much more pressure than the short trip to the lungs. So its muscular wall is about three times thicker than the right's.
asks: Tell me about the left heart

faq.q: What does the right side of the heart do?
faq.a: The right side collects blood coming back from the body, low in oxygen, and pumps it to the lungs to pick up oxygen and get rid of carbon dioxide.
asks: Tell me about the right heart
Which side of the heart pumps to the lungs?

faq.q: What happens to blood in the lungs?
faq.a: In the lungs blood unloads carbon dioxide into the air sacs and loads up with oxygen, which red blood cells carry back to the left side of the heart.

faq.q: Why does blood go through the heart twice?
faq.a: After squeezing through the tiny vessels of the lungs, blood loses pressure. Sending it back to the heart for a second pump gives it the push to reach the whole body quickly.
No. Blood is always red: bright red when full of oxygen and darker red when low in oxygen. Veins only look blue because of how light passes through skin.

facts: The left ventricle wall is roughly three times thicker than the right ventricle wall.
Humans have a double circulation: pulmonary, to the lungs, and systemic, to the body.
